clue.text: Singular snack from dodgy pier bars

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or out of order, so these letters are not to be trusted in their printed sequence

blocks.note: the letters of both words, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone buys a one-off nibble from the questionable bars on a seaside pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like it means odd, but it simply says the snack is one rib rather than ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare rib is a single cut of pork rib, typically eaten as a finger-food snack.

clue.text: Credit goddess with calamity

blocks.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts
Isis is the Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: A goddess who brings credit also brings disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or disaster, so it serves as a synonym for calamity.

clue.text: Underdog's leader surrounded by artillery at Ypres' first place for the dead

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the one at the front, so only its opening letter is wanted
being surrounded means lying inside something else, so one piece goes within the other
first points to the opening letter of the place name just before it

blocks.note: a mortar is a piece of artillery
opening letter of Underdog
opening letter of Ypres

explanation.surface: A grim First World War scene: shelling at Ypres and a place to lay out the fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside MORTAR to make MORTUAR, then Y is added to give MORTUARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is a building or room where corpses are kept before burial or cremation.

clue.text: Queen gets in to make very hot beefy drink

indicators.note: getting in means entering something, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to boil is to heat a liquid until it bubbles
VR is Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The Queen arrives to heat up a cup of something meaty.
explanation.walkthrough: VR, for Victoria Regina, is a common crossword Queen alongside ER. Bovril is a British brand of beef extract, often made into a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovril is a salty beef extract that is dissolved in hot water and drunk as a savoury beverage.

clue.text: Unionist politician's anger with sporting official

blocks.note: U is an abbreviation for Unionist
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the 's is the joining 'has'
ire is a literary word for anger

explanation.surface: A Unionist MP loses their temper with a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire officiates in sports such as cricket and tennis, enforcing the rules of play.

clue.text: "Tribune" vendor's bowels are irregular

indicators.note: bowels are the innards of something, so the letters are taken from inside the printed words

blocks.note: found across the end of the newspaper's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: The newspaper seller suffers from irregular bowel movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven is not smooth or consistent, the same sense as irregular.

clue.text: Girl has responsibility to get a shrub

blocks.note: Jo is a girl's name
a job can mean a duty or task one is responsible for
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is put in charge of fetching a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Jojoba is a desert shrub of the American southwest, grown for the oil in its seeds.

clue.text: Highlight account with little money

blocks.note: AC is a standard abbreviation for account
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A bank statement draws attention to how little money is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To accent something is to emphasise or draw attention to it, as a verb synonym of highlight.

clue.text: Get severe burns from this type of interrogation?

definitions.text: Get severe burns from this type of interrogation

blocks.note: the surface reading: the most serious grade of burn injury
the setter's reading: the name of an intense, gruelling questioning

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase names both the worst classification of burn and a harsh grilling, so the clue pretends the interrogation actually scorches the suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the third degree means subjecting them to prolonged, aggressive questioning; the same phrase grades the deepest burns.

clue.text: Return to have sex with retired teacher and it's rubbish!

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word is read from right to left
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so this title is also read backwards

blocks.note: to bed someone is to have sex with them
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation at someone going back to sleep with an old schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or broken remains, which is what rubbish means here as a noun.

clue.text: Sporting achievement of a journalist claiming race ahead of first and third of riders

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the journalist encloses what follows
ahead of says the race comes in front of the letters that follow it
only the letters in positions one and three of the next word are kept

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, often a mediocre one
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
the first letter of riders
the third letter of riders

explanation.surface: A reporter covers a horse race and celebrates a rider's triple success.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race; 'a journalist' is the outer piece, split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-trick is three successes in a row by one player, such as three goals in a match.

clue.text: Soundly trim fruit

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: to pare is to trim by cutting away the edges

explanation.surface: Neatly cut up some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet, juicy tree fruit, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Simplify second part of transport infrastructure around the centre of Leeds

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the infrastructure piece wraps round what follows
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letter of the city is kept

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a tramline is the rail a tram runs on
Leeds has five letters, the middle one being its third

explanation.surface: A plan to tidy up a stretch of Leeds's tram network.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England; its middle letter lands just after the second letter of the tram piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to make a process simpler and more efficient by removing unnecessary steps.

clue.text: Began a synod badly with discipline of doctors

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: A church council meeting got off to a poor start because of a disciplinary matter among doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discipline' looks like punishment in the church setting, but here it means a branch of study. Obs and gynae is the British shorthand for obstetrics and gynaecology.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics and gynaecology is a medical specialty dealing with childbirth and women's reproductive health.

clue.text: The Spanish upset the French with bloody symbolic art

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the Spanish article is read bottom to top

blocks.note: la is a Spanish word for 'the'
le is a French word for 'the'
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: A bloodthirsty piece of symbolism that annoys the Spanish and the French alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish article is LA here, not EL; turned over it gives AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a work of art or story whose characters and events stand symbolically for hidden meanings.

clue.text: Suddenly and deftly swallowing pint after game

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the adverb holds the other pieces within it
after places the pint behind the game in the inner piece

blocks.note: ably means skilfully
RU is rugby union
PT is the abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: Someone neatly downs a pint straight after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' is rugby union here, a common crossword abbreviation; 'after' only orders the two inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Abruptly means without warning, so it is an adverb synonym of suddenly.

clue.text: Good lodgings for lads in stables

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
rooms can mean rented accommodation

explanation.surface: Decent accommodation is provided for the young stable workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooms are people employed to look after horses, traditionally called stable lads in Britain.

clue.text: Woman drowning in G&T: greedy thing!

indicators.note: someone drowning in a drink is submerged inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the drink gin and tonic, as its two letters
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman overindulging in gin and tonics is scolded as a glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gannet is a greedy eater, from the seabird's reputation for gulping fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannet is informal British slang for a person who eats greedily, named after the voracious seabird.

clue.text: Language, not Norse, in which composer gives account of journey

indicators.note: not tells us something is excluded, so that letter is dropped from the word
in which says the following name sits inside the trimmed word

blocks.note: a tongue is a language
N is the abbreviation for Norse
Maurice Ravel, the French composer

explanation.surface: A composer writes a narrative of travels in a tongue other than Norse.
explanation.walkthrough: Once the Norse letter is gone, the French composer sits after the first letter of what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelogue is a film, talk or book describing someone's travels.

clue.text: Some returned for clever alternative to zip

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a run within the printed words
returned means sent back, so that run is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run spanning the end of the first word and most of the second

explanation.surface: Some shrewd people have come back with a better fastener than the zip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For clever' read backwards is REVELC ROF, and the six letters needed sit inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Velcro is a hook-and-loop fastener used on clothing and bags where a zip might otherwise be.

clue.text: Attention surrounding St Edmund's head in festival

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so the first piece wraps round the rest
the head of a name is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
taken as written
first letter of Edmund

explanation.surface: A feast day honouring the saint involves attention to St Edmund's head.
explanation.walkthrough: St Edmund was an English king and martyr whose severed head, legend says, was found guarded by a wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Pole keeping a track

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the pole holds the other letter inside it

blocks.note: a rod is a pole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A post keeping a path marked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A road can be any route or way, and a track is a rough road or path.

clue.text: Messy blue goo found round northern French city

indicators.note: something messy is disordered, so these letters are scrambled
being found round something means enclosing it, so the scrambled letters go around the extra one

blocks.note: the letters of both words
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A sticky blue slime has turned up in a town in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulogne-sur-Mer is a port city on the Channel coast of northern France.

clue.text: Adopting a laid-back attitude to drink in Europe

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: Taking it easy about drinking while on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but simply supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying face upward, and figuratively passive or inactive, a literally laid-back posture.

clue.text: Arrest dishevelled philosopher

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy and disordered, so these letters are messed up

blocks.note: the six letters as printed

explanation.surface: Police detain a scruffy thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist philosopher, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Lapdog, say, keeps distance from ball

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the pet holds the measure inside

blocks.note: a lapdog is an example of a pet; 'say' marks the example
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A little dog stays well away from a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small rounded mass, a tiny ball of compressed material or shot.
